sources.note: Nothing. Single mention: maski 'also occurred in Kiautschou Pidgin German, which was spoken in the German colony Kiautschou on the coast of China in the early 20th century (Mühlhäusler 2011: 194)'. Its bibliography supplies the full citation of Mühlhäusler 2011 (list of works to obtain).

sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 2017. Varieties of language policies and their consequences in the German colonies of the Pacific area. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, Special Issue 2017 (Maitz & Volker, eds., Language Contact in the German Colonies), 9-26.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Language-policy paper; 26 mentions of Kiautschou (demography, schools, germanisation) but no linguistic description of the pidgin; a full-text search for stress/accent/phonolog/prosod returns nothing.

sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 1983. Notes on the Pidgin German of Kiautschou. In L. Carrington, J. Siegel, P. Mühlhäusler et al. (eds.), Papers in Pidgin and Creole Linguistics No. 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-65), 139-142. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A65.139
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only primary description (4 pp.); explicitly based on 'only second-hand evidence': four written sentences quoted from Hesse-Wartegg 1898, Kiautschou-Post 1911/1912 and a 1915 novel. Only phonological remarks (p. 141): 'reduction of consonant clusters (nich for nicht)' and 'the stereotype confusion of l and r'. No section on phonology, no mention of stress, accent or prosody.

sources.citation: Hesse-Wartegg, Ernst von. 1898. Schantung und Deutsch-China. Leipzig: J. J. Weber. (archive.org scanned, id schantungunddeu00wargoog)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Travel book; p. 10 contains the one attested sentence ('Ik sabe deutch.. Gobenol at gebene pamischu open Otel, kommen Sie, luksi, no hebe pisi man, no habe dima, bei an bei') with the author's gloss of the Pidgin-English words. No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 2011. Deutsch schümpfen, chinese schümpfen, plenty sabbi - Die deutsche Sprache in Kiautschou. In Thomas Stolz, Christina Vossmann & Barbara Dewein (eds.), Kolonialzeitliche Sprachforschung. Die Beschreibung afrikanischer und ozeanischer Sprachen zur Zeit der deutschen Kolonialherrschaft, 187-202. Berlin: Akademie Verlag.

sources.note: The fullest treatment (16 pp.) of German and Pidgin German in Kiautschou, cited by Engelberg & Stolberg 2017 (p. 194) for pidgin lexical items; the only work that could add attestations beyond the four sentences of 1983. Unlikely to contain a stress statement given the written-only corpus, but must be checked to close the file.
